paraphrase: Case 1: Emperor Wu asks the first principle of the holy truths — Bodhidharma: 'vast emptiness, nothing holy'; 'who faces me?' — 'I don't know'. Yuanwu comments that Bodhidharma came by sea because he saw Mahāyāna capacities here, 'singly transmitting the mind-seal, not establishing words and letters, pointing directly at the human mind, seeing the nature and becoming buddha'.

paraphrase: Case 12, 'three pounds of flax': Yuanwu warns that many misunderstand this case — some say Dongshan was weighing flax, others that he answered east when asked west; words are only vehicles of the Way; seeking the meaning in the phrase one will not see it even in a dream until Maitreya comes.

paraphrase: Yuanwu's pointer to case 12: the sword that kills and the sword that gives life is the ancient standard and today's pivot; in killing not a hair is harmed, in giving life one loses body and life; 'the one road upward the thousand sages do not transmit' — yet why so many entangling cases? Case 12 follows: 'what is buddha?' — Dongshan: 'three pounds of flax'.
